content:
We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically to the given molecule (target) reproduces the Peterson reaction: formation of alkene from beta-hydroxy silane elimination. The forward reaction: beta-hydroxy silane -> alkene + Si group + carbonyl? Actually Peterson: alpha-silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl forming beta-hydroxy silane, then elimination gives alkene, losing Si-O bond and forming C=C. So in retrosynthesis, we need to break C=C (formed) and generate a beta-hydroxy silane precursor (i.e., a carbonyl + silyl group). So functional groups: C-C double bond formed, ketone broken? The description says ketones and trimethylsilyl groups are lost. So forward: ketone + TMSCH2- (alpha-silyl carbanion) -> beta-hydroxy silane -> alkene + Si-O bond broken, carbonyl broken? Actually ketone is broken (C=O broken) to give alkene. So in retrosynthesis, we need to break C=C and form a carbonyl (ketone) and a trimethylsilyl group attached to carbon (maybe as TMSCH2-). So we need a template that breaks C=C double bond and forms a carbonyl (ketone) and a trimethylsilyl group.

Thus we can search template catalog with criteria: functional_groups_broken: "C-C double bonds" (since forward forms double bond, retrosynthesis breaks it). functional_groups_formed: "ketones", "trimethylsilyl". Also bonds broken: C-Si? Actually forward breaks C-Si and C-O, but retrosynthesis forms them. So bonds_formed: maybe "C-Si", "C-O". But we can try minimal criteria: broken functional group = "C-C double bonds", formed functional groups = "ketones", "trimethylsilyl". Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria.
